'''Tomoyuki Arakawa''' (Japanese: {{lang|ja|荒川 知幸}}; born 22 May 1968) is a Japanese mathematician, mathematical physicist, and a professor at the RIMS of the [[Kyoto University]]. His research interests are [[representation theory]] and [[vertex algebras]] and he is known especially for the work in [[W-algebra]]s.
He obtained his PhD from the [[Nagoya University|University of Nagoya]] in 1999. In 2018 he was invited speaker at the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] in Rio de Janeiro.<ref>{{Cite web |title=ICM 2018 INVITED LECTURES ToC |url=https://impa.br/icm2018/invited-toc.html |access-date=13 August 2022 |website=impa.br}}</ref> He won the [[MSJ Autumn Prize]] in 2017 for his work on representation theory of W-algebras.<ref>{{Cite web |title=The 2017 MSJ Autumn Prize |url=https://www.mathsoc.jp/en/publicity/autumn2017-en.html |access-date=13 August 2022 |website=The Mathematical Society of Japan}}</ref>
